examples.title: Basic
examples.description: The smallest possible table: four rows, six columns, no state.

examples.title: Basic (External State)
examples.description: The table state lives in your model and you can inspect, reset, and replace it.

examples.title: Basic (Dynamic Columns)
examples.description: Columns built at runtime from the data's own keys.

examples.title: Header Groups
examples.description: Nested column groups rendered as multi-row headers and footers.

examples.title: Kitchen Sink (All Features)
examples.description: Every feature on one table: sorting, filtering, grouping, expanding, selection, pinning, visibility, ordering, sizing, pagination.

examples.title: Cell Selection
examples.description: Rectangular cell ranges with click, shift-click, ctrl-click, and keyboard movement.

examples.title: Cell Spanning
examples.description: Merge adjacent cells with row and column spans.

examples.title: Column Filters
examples.description: Per-column text and range filters plus a global filter.

examples.title: Column Filters (Faceted)
examples.description: Filter inputs driven by faceted unique values and min/max.

examples.title: Bucketed Faceted Filters
examples.description: Faceted values grouped into buckets for numeric and date columns.

examples.title: Fuzzy Search Filters
examples.description: A custom fuzzy filter function with match ranking.

examples.title: Column Ordering
examples.description: Reorder columns through state.

examples.title: Column Ordering (DnD)
examples.description: Drag headers to reorder columns using HTML5 drag events.

examples.title: Column Pinning
examples.description: Pin columns to the left or right edge.

examples.title: Column Pinning (Split)
examples.description: Pinned regions rendered as three separate tables.

examples.title: Sticky Column Pinning
examples.description: Pinned columns stay put with position: sticky while the rest scroll.

examples.title: Column Sizing
examples.description: Column widths from state with min and max clamping.

examples.title: Column Resizing
examples.description: Drag a header edge to resize a column, with onChange and onEnd modes and left-to-right or right-to-left direction.

examples.title: Performant Column Resizing
examples.description: Resize with the body rendered from CSS variables so only the header re-renders while dragging.

examples.title: Column Visibility
examples.description: Show and hide columns with checkboxes.

examples.title: Expanding
examples.description: Nested sub-rows with expand and collapse.

examples.title: Expanding Sub Components
examples.description: Expand a row to reveal arbitrary content instead of sub-rows.

examples.title: Grouping
examples.description: Group rows by one or more columns.

examples.title: Aggregation
examples.description: Aggregated values on group rows and in footers.

examples.title: Grouped Aggregation
examples.description: Nested groups with merged aggregates at every level.

examples.title: Pagination
examples.description: Client-side pages with page size, page jump, and counts.

examples.title: Row DnD
examples.description: Drag rows to reorder the underlying data using HTML5 drag events.

examples.title: Row Pinning
examples.description: Pin rows to the top or bottom of the table.

examples.title: Row Selection
examples.description: Checkbox selection with all, some, and per-row state.

examples.title: Sorting
examples.description: Click and shift-click headers for single and multi-column sorting.

examples.title: Virtualized Rows
examples.description: 50,000 sorted and filtered rows rendered through an Elm virtual list.

examples.title: Virtualized Columns
examples.description: Wide tables: only the columns in view are rendered.

examples.title: Infinite Scrolling
examples.description: Pages of rows fetched as you scroll, appended to the data and re-run through the pipeline.

examples.title: Realtime Trading
examples.description: Prices updating on a timer while sorting and filtering stay live.
